_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS THE PATH-SCOPE LAWS ARE NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- \
crates/mnemosyne-cli/sweeps/citation-path-scope.sweep.json
WHAT IT IS ABOUT. `validate-code-refs --paths <file>...` is SCE lift-request
4-B: a run narrowed to the files a commit touched, judging the axes that one
file plus the store can decide, and SAYING SO about the ones it cannot. Six
tests in `validate_code_refs_path_scope.rs` and three in `code_refs.rs` state
those laws, and they shipped green — which says the laws hold and says
nothing about whether they could break. Each injection below breaks ONE READ
and names the tests that must go red for it.
FOUR ROUNDS ARE IN HERE NOW, not one. Rounds 1142, 1143 and 1144 wrote nine
more laws on the same surface and every one of them also shipped green: the
symbol axis says whether it had an instrument (`symbol_axis_reach.rs`), the
argument spellings a hook produces are the file they name
(`path_scope_arguments.rs`), and a symbol claim no resolver covers stops the
run. Those rounds found two REAL defects by writing a failing test first — a
no-resolver run publishing `symbol_mismatch_count: 0`, and the same run
exiting 0 — and the rest of their laws have no evidence at all beyond being
green on first write. That is what this file is for.
SCOPE IS THE WHOLE WORKSPACE. The edits land in `mnemosyne-validate` and in
`mnemosyne-cli`, and Round 1139 measured what a narrower run costs: under
`-p mnemosyne-cli` the EDITED CRATE'S OWN SUITE never runs, so a law its unit
tests already guard and a law nothing guards come back as the same red set.
`--workspace` is the widest reading of the population that can go red.
THE RED SETS BELOW ARE MEASURED (Round 1145), not predicted. One full run of
this file on this tree: CONTROL 1870 passed, 0 failed, 161 targets, and every
`expect_red` replaced with what that run reported. Fifteen of the sixteen
injections fired with `missed` empty — the laws of Rounds 1141 through 1144
are not vacuous, and that is a fact about a run rather than about an author's
expectation. Cost: 3h30m of suites.
THAT CONTROL IS FOR A COMMAND THIS FILE NO LONGER RUNS (Round 1171). The
line above was measured under `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, which
MEASURED on this tree is 1956 tests where the same workspace with its
features is 1965: nine live in the server's `#![cfg(feature)]` targets, and
a feature that is off compiles those to an empty test binary rather than to
an error. CI covers them in a second job; a sweep has one command and cannot,
so an injection only those nine would catch was scored here as a law that
cannot break. The command now carries `--all-features` and the control above
is STALE BY EXACTLY THAT DIFFERENCE — treat 1870/161 as the old suite's
number until a full run replaces it. `expect_red` is unaffected: `red_set`
is the default `at-least`, so a wider suite may redden more and must still
redden every name below.
A NUMBER WITHOUT ITS COMMAND IS A TRAP, and this one sprang: the session
that wrote this paragraph read 1870/161 against its own `--all-features`
1965/155 and spent an hour on a discrepancy that was two suites, not a
defect. Round 1139 already wrote the rule — a measurement carries its own
population — and a control line in a manifest is a measurement.
ROUND 1165 CLOSED THE SIXTEENTH, AND THE PARAGRAPH BELOW IS KEPT AS THE
HISTORY OF IT RATHER THAN AS THE STATE. The repair was the FIXTURE, and it
was found by asking the question the injection asks as a LAW instead of as
a sweep: `every_fixture_reads_differently_under_a_grammar_that_is_not_its
_own` runs every other shipped backend over each fixture's cited line and
requires the reading to differ. It named five colliding pairs — the Go
fixture under C++, and the Kotlin fixture under both C++ and Python — and
the Rust one it was written for had already been repaired by Round 1146's
rebuild, so the paragraph below had been stale for twenty rounds. Go now
cites inside a grouped `var` and Kotlin inside an `object`, both shapes the
other grammars cannot name. MEASURED: with this injection applied by hand,
five tests go red — the two named below plus
`backends::tests::each_row_builds_the_plugin_it_names` (which the note
below correctly said was unmeasured), the new fixture law, and
`every_backend_this_build_ships_resolves_its_own_language`. That run was
`-p mnemosyne-cli --lib --test symbol_axis_reach`, so it is a subset of
this sweep's `--workspace` and the three extra names are not added to
`expect_red`: under `at-least` they would pass, but an entry here is a
claim about a full run and nobody has done one since.
(HISTORY) IT WAS `at-least`, AND THE REASON WAS THE SIXTEENTH INJECTION.
`the-wire-hands-rust-the-other-languages-resolver` reddened NOTHING: handing
the `rust` key the C++ resolver leaves all 1870 tests green. Under
`exhaustive` an empty `expect_red` is refused at read time (Round 1140), and
it should be — an injection that reddens nothing is the one outcome a sweep
exists to detect rather than to declare. So its aim stays written down, the
harness keeps failing this sweep while it goes unreached, and promotion waits
on the repair rather than on a list edit.
WHY THAT ONE MISSED, since it is the finding: the fixture's `fn alpha() { … }`
is ALSO a valid C++ function definition — return type `fn`, name `alpha` — so
both resolvers answer `alpha` and the test cannot tell which one ran. The
spelling of a fixture is what makes it a control (Round 1096), and Round
1142's claim that the config-to-plugin wire now has a reader was measured
false here.
THE PREDICTION THAT HELD: the axis-verdict map is read by the scan (as its
skip conditions) and by the report (as its `not_judged` list), and
`the-report-stops-naming-the-axes-it-skipped` cuts only the second reader. It
reddened seven suites. Had the two drifted into separate derivations it would
have reddened nothing — which is exactly what the sixteenth one did.

injections.name: the-scope-stops-narrowing-the-read-set
injections.why: the scope exists to make the run read fewer files; with the filter gone a scoped run answers about the whole tree while still calling itself scoped, which is the equality law's exact negation

injections.name: a-scoped-run-judges-the-spec-side-anyway
injections.why: the spec-side axes ask whether a store claim has a witness ANYWHERE; judged against a partial read set every binding outside the scope looks unwitnessed, so this is the false-reject a consumer's hook would eat

edits.to: } else if false && scoped && axis.side() == AuditSide::Spec {

injections.name: the-report-stops-naming-the-axes-it-skipped
injections.why: an axis nobody judged and an axis that found nothing print the same silence; the naming is the whole difference, and three suites beyond the scope tests read it

injections.name: an-axis-nobody-measured-publishes-a-zero
injections.why: this is the defect in its original form — three modes printed `0` for an axis they structurally skip, and `0` is the answer a judged-and-clean axis gives; the rejection message is downstream of the same map, so it goes back to printing the zero too

injections.name: a-file-this-gate-never-reads-is-filed-as-absent
injections.why: 'no configured path covers it' and 'it is not on disk' are two different pieces of news for a hook handing over a changed-file list, and only one of them is the consumer's typo

injections.name: the-narrowing-vanishes-from-the-human-report
injections.why: the consumer reads a terminal; a scoped run whose short violation list is the only evidence of narrowing looks exactly like a clean whole-tree run

injections.name: the-resolver-goes-back-to-the-disk
injections.why: the point of passing the source is that the symbol answer comes from the bytes the citation was extracted from; a plugin that reads the path again has its own copy, and two reads of one file can disagree. Round 1152 moved the walk out of the per-language crates into mnemosyne-plugin-tree-sitter-core, so this injection now lands ONCE and reaches all five backends rather than only Rust's — and the anchor it used to name stopped existing, which is exactly the decay the sweeps gate catches (Round 1156). Its expect_red is a LOWER BOUND, as every entry here is until the set is promoted: the listed Rust tests still go red because they resolve through a path that does not exist, and so now do the other four backends' and the engine's own

injections.name: the-file-is-put-to-the-resolver-one-citation-at-a-time
injections.why: this is the 108.9-second defect itself: the demand is batched per file, and a call that carries only the first line is the shape the batching replaced

injections.name: the-census-prices-every-bound-citation-instead-of-the-checked-ones
injections.why: a census that counts `cited and bound` rather than `records a symbol` overstates the axis's cost, and the consumer's payoff estimate is a division by exactly this number

injections.name: the-axis-with-no-instrument-goes-back-to-publishing-a-zero
injections.why: Round 1142's whole subject: with the resolver map empty the scan collects symbol demand and puts it to nobody, and before that round the report published `0` for it — the answer a judged and clean axis gives, in the mode the consumer reaches by deleting their resolver blocks to price the axis

edits.to: } else if false && axis == AuditAxis::SymbolMismatch && self.symbol_resolvers.is_empty()

injections.name: the-wire-hands-rust-the-other-languages-resolver
injections.why: the config-to-plugin wire had no reader until Round 1142 — the one test that configured a buildable backend asserted only exit 0, so a registry keyed to the wrong resolver resolved nothing and passed; this is that miskeying. Round 1151 moved the wire out of an if/else chain in main.rs into the backend TABLE, so the miskeying now lands in the table's `rust` row and the anchor it used to name stopped existing (found by the sweeps gate, Round 1156). The move also gave the pairing a second reader — `backends::tests::each_row_builds_the_plugin_it_names` asks each row's constructor which plugin it built — but whether that test fires under this injection is UNMEASURED, so it is not listed below: an expect_red entry is a claim, and a claim about a run nobody has done belongs in prose

injections.name: a-symbol-claim-nobody-can-check-is-let-through
injections.why: Round 1144 — a section recording a symbol for a language no resolver covers is a claim nobody checks, and letting it through is what made deleting a resolver block a way to pass rather than a way to measure

injections.name: the-refusal-counts-unreached-files-instead-of-unchecked-claims
injections.why: the boundary law 3 guards: `unresolved_languages` counts FILES and `unchecked_citations` counts CLAIMS, and widening the refusal from the second to the first refuses every adopter holding a second language for prose they never wrote

injections.name: a-dot-slash-prefix-stops-naming-the-file
injections.why: a hook that walks with `find` hands `./src/a.rs`; a scope that keeps the prefix matches no file, judges nothing, and exits 0 reporting a clean tree — the failure this mode exists to prevent, arriving through the argument instead of the axis

injections.name: a-directory-selects-only-a-file-named-exactly
injections.why: the reply promises a directory is everything under it; without the prefix match a directory selects nothing at all, which is again a scope that runs, judges no file and reports clean

injections.name: the-scan-emits-what-the-verdict-map-says-it-skipped
injections.why: the run self-checks that a not-judged axis emitted nothing, and a self-check with no reader is the shape this project keeps finding; here the map still says `not judged` while step 3 runs, so the check must stop the run rather than let a consistent-looking report out
